q: According to the Bergonie-Tribondeau law, rapidly dividing undifferentiated cells are the most radiosensitive. Of these options the most radiosensitive cell is:
ex: Spermatogonia divide rapidly and are among the most radiosensitive cells of the body.

q: A radiographer at distance d from a point photon source walks to distance 2d. The exposure rate relative to the original becomes:
ex: A point source follows the inverse-square law; doubling the distance cuts the exposure to a quarter.

q: Routine personal dosimetry of diagnostic radiology personnel in India is monitored today with which device?
ex: A LiF thermoluminescent dosimeter now serves individual monitoring of staff, replacing film badges.

q: Which agent introduced the first non-ionic water-soluble iodinated contrast into clinical use?
ex: Metrizamide was the first non-ionic contrast; diatrizoate is an older ionic molecule.

q: A patient with eGFR 35 ml/min needs iodinated contrast for CT with hydration run. Which agent carries the lowest risk of contrast-induced nephropathy?
ex: Iodixanol (iso-osmolar dimer) is associated with the lowest CIN rate among iodinated agents.

q: Which gadolinium-based compound is safest in a patient with coexisting advanced renal failure, minimising the risk of nephrogenic systemic fibrosis?
ex: Macrocyclic chelates release far less free gadolinium and carry the least NSF risk; linear agents are contraindicated in renal impairment.

q: A preterm newborn with grunting and retractions has a film of widespread ground-glass granularity plus air bronchograms and over-aeration. The most consistent diagnosis is:
ex: RDS appears as fine ground-glass granularity with air bronchograms; transient tachypnoea differs.

q: On a supine abdominal radiograph of a baby, free intra-peritoneal air gathers under the anterior abdominal wall and outlines the whole cavity as an oval gas collection. Which sign is this?
ex: The oval of gas under the ventral wall in a supine neonate is the football sign; Rigler sign is loop lamination.

q: A newborn who fails to pass meconium has an iodine enema showing a contracted narrow rectosigmoid that cones into a dilated colon. The diagnosis is:
ex: A spastic aganglionic segment with a transition cone on the enema typifies Hirschsprung disease.

q: Foamy granular opacities in a distended newborn's right upper abdomen plus a colon of normal width favours:
ex: Soap-bubble meconium blended high in the abdomen with no mechanical block points to meconium ileus; a water-soluble enema treats it.

q: A normal newborn film shows a triangular opacity in the superior right mediastinum, most prominent in inspiration. What is it?
ex: The sail sign of the thymus is a normal neonatal thoracic finding that changes shape and size.

q: A head-injured patient is briefly conscious then comatose. NCCT shows a biconvex lentiform hyperdensity respecting the skull sutures. The diagnosis is:
ex: The lucid interval plus a biconvex suture-respecting bleed are the signature of extradural haematoma.

q: A week after a fall an anticoagulated elderly patient presents with confusion and half-side weakness. The CT shows a concave crescent of subdensity sweeping across suture lines. The best next step is:
ex: A concave crescentic subacute subdural effuses the convexity brain; burr-hole drainage relieves the pressure.

q: A patient is scanned 90 minutes after acute-onset hemiplegia; the plain CT is essentially normal. Which sequence demonstrates the early infarct most sensitively?
ex: DWI catches cytotoxic oedema within minutes of occlusion; FLAIR and T2 turn positive much later.

q: Sudden thunderclap headache and a rigid neck; the CT shows hyperdense basal cisterns and convexity sulci. What is the diagnosis?
ex: Fissural hyperdensity in the cisterns and sulci after thunderclap is acute subarachnoid haemorrhage.

q: A febrile patient with seizures has an MRI ring-enhancing mass whose core is bright on the diffusion sequence. The most likely lesion:
ex: Pus restricts diffusion, so the abscess core stays bright on DWI whereas necrotic tumour does not.

q: MRI shows a snowman-shaped mass expanding the sella and rising above it, compressing the optic chiasm. The likely diagnosis:
ex: An hour-glass sella-suprasellar mass lifting the chiasm with a snowman waist is a pituitary macroadenoma.

q: An extra-axial dural-based enhancing mass with broad base and hyperostosis of the adjacent vault on CT is classically:
ex: Uniformly enhancing extra-axial dural mass with dural tail and local hyperostosis is a meningioma.

q: An infant with mild cyanosis and heart failure has a chest film showing a cardiac silhouette shaped like a snowman on a pedestal. Which diagnosis best fits this configuration?
ex: In supracardiac TAPVR the dilated vertical vein and SVC give the classic snowman or figure-of-eight sign on the film.

q: A construction mason with a chisel chip suspects an intraocular metallic foreign body in the eye. Which imaging study must be avoided?
ex: A ferromagnetic intraocular fragment may be displaced and torque inside the globe; MRI is contraindicated until its nature is screened.

q: An expanded and totally opacified frontal sinus with a thin intact wall evolves over weeks of frontal headache. Diagnosis:
ex: A mucocoele is a sinus inflated by ostial obstruction that expands and can erode the orbital plate.

q: Dysphonia with an apical lung opacity that destroys the first two ribs in a long smoker points to:
ex: Apical mass with rib erosion and Horner plus arm pain is the superior sulcus Pancoast tumour.

q: A child with a murmur has a film showing very plethoric (engorged) lung fields plus a prominent main pulmonary segment. This suggests:
o: A left-to-right shunt such as VSD or PDA
ex: Left-to-right shunting floods the lung; cyanosed tetralogy leaves lung fields oligaemic.

q: A PA film in a dyspnoeic woman shows a bulge of the left atrial appendage and upward displacement of the left main bronchus; a barium swallow is pushed gently backward. This corresponds to:
ex: A left atrium of size lifts the bronchus, bulges the appendage and indents the oesophagus on swallow.

q: A swallow study in a woman with months of progressive food dysphagia shows a dilated oesophagus that ends in a smooth narrowed beak at the cardia with slow emptying. Diagnosis:
ex: A dilated oesophagus tapering to a smooth beak at the cardia with delayed emptying fits achalasia.

q: Low-grade fever with an ileocaecal stricture, a contracted scarred caecum and a central contrast fleck on barium in a young Indian adult:
ex: A goblet caecum with terminal-ileal narrowing is the ileocaecal-TB pattern of a febrile young adult.

q: A 3-month-old with projectile vomiting after each feed has a pyloric ultrasound showing muscle wall thickness of 4.5 mm and an elongated narrowed canal. Diagnosis:
ex: Pyloric wall >3-4 mm with a stretched channel on US confirms hypertrophic pyloric stenosis.

q: For a child with blunt abdominal trauma whose supine film is without free air, the most useful additional view to expose a GI perforation is:
ex: Erect and decubitus films pool the free gas under a diaphragm that the supine film misses.

q: A woman notes a gurgling lump in the neck during swallowing and regurgitates food eaten the previous day. The barium swallow shows a pouch of the hypopharynx just above the cricopharyngeus. Diagnosis:
ex: Zenker diverticulum arises above the cricopharyngeus in the pharynx and retains old food, causing late regurgitation.

q: An elderly obstructed patient has a plain film and CT showing abundant intraluminal gas, air lucencies over the hepatic shadow and a remote calcified stone lodged in a mid small-bowel loop. The unifying diagnosis is:
ex: Pneumobilia meeting a calcified obstructing stone is the classic gallstone ileus (Rigler triad).

q: A limping adolescent has an expansile soap-bubble lucency of the proximal humeral metaphysis with a paper-thin blown-out cortex and no matrix. Diagnosis:
ex: A multiloculated soap-bubble blow-out metaphyseal lesion of the young is an aneurysmal bone cyst.

q: A growing teen limps after running; the frog-lateral view shows the proximal femoral head slipping backward and medially in the neck. The diagnosis is:
ex: SCFE shows a medial and posterior slipping of the femoral epiphysis best seen on the frog-lateral projection.

q: A teenager with a nagging knee has a lytic focus in the epiphysis of the distal femur containing small faint specks of calcific density. Diagnosis:
ex: Lucent epiphyseal lesion with flecks of chondroid matrix in the young is a chondroblastoma.

q: An exophytic bony mound on a long bone with cortex and marrow continuous with the host bone and a direction away from the nearest joint describes:
ex: Osteochondroma keeps cortex and cancellous marrow continuous with the host and grows away from the joint.

q: A 70-year-old with pelvic pain after a trivial fall has a bone scan showing an H-shaped double tracer band across the sacral alae. The diagnosis:
ex: The bilateral H of tracer in both sacral alae (Honda sign) marks insufficiency sacral fractures.

q: A menopausal woman has knee pain and a decisive dense line of calcium in the meniscus and hyaline cartilage of the joint on the radiograph. The deposited crystal is:
ex: Chondrocalcinosis seen as dense cartilage lines is the CP-PD of pseudo-gout.

q: A 30-year-old man with ascending stiffness and repeated uveitis has a single lateral film that shows the whole spine with continuous bridging ossification. The unified diagnosis is:
ex: Complete syndesmophyte bridging of the spine (bamboo spine) with sacroiliitis is ankylosing spondylitis.

q: A KUB of a patient with repeated urinary infections shows a branched stone casting the whole pelvicalyceal tree. The usual composition is:
ex: A branched staghorn replicating the pelvis is usually struvite from urease-producing infection.

q: In a renal-colic emergency, the single best test to show the site, size and whether a ureterolith is present is:
o: Unenhanced CT of the urinary tract
ex: Non-contrast CT of the whole urinary tract images stones with high sensitivity and sizes them.

q: In a child with repeated infections, the test that demonstrates vesico-ureteric reflux while the child voids is:
ex: Micturating cystographic fill and void directly shows refluxing contrast into the ureters.

q: A bulky redundant renal pelvis with a long narrow pleat at the ureteric junction shown on an IVU in a young adult means:
ex: A distended pelvis with a delicate narrowed junction defines a PUJ obstruction.

q: A liver ultrasound displays a well-defined cyst containing folded undulating strands of membrane lying curled within. Which sign is this?
ex: The water lily sign from a detached endocyst membrane within the cyst is seen in hydatid (Echinococcus).

q: A young hypertensive with a short segment of rigid bean-pod beading over the mid renal artery at aortography contains:
ex: Multifocal beading of the renal artery in a young hypertensive is the classic fibromuscular dysplasia.

q: A young hypoxic patient with pleuritic chest pain has a chest film showing a local lucent oligaemic patch in one zone and a prominent pulmonary trunk. The event most likely responsible is:
ex: The Westermark sign of regional oligaemia and an enlarged pulmonary artery is a strong hint for acute PE.

q: In a patient with a pre-existing upper-lobe cavity from old tuberculosis, a new fungal ball fills the cavity and a crescent of air separates it from the cavity wall on the radiograph. The lesion is:
ex: The air-crescent (Monod) sign between the fungus ball and the cavity wall is typical of an aspergiloma.

q: Contrast CT shows an enhancing liver mass that extends as thrombus into the inferior vena cava and portal vein. Which hepatic neoplasm has this characteristic vascular extension?
ex: The hepatocellular carcinoma classically invades the veins, occluding them with its dysplastic thrombus.
